name: Caleb and Joshua
charge: Wholly following the Lord when ten spies and the whole congregation would not
summary: Twelve men saw the same land, the same walled cities and the same giants. Ten said they were not able. Two rent their clothes before a congregation reaching for stones and said the Lord was with them and they need not fear the people. The Most High had already said He would deliver the enemy into their hands, so the stature of the giants did not matter. Caleb had another spirit with him and followed the Lord fully; of six hundred thousand, these two walked into the land.
offenseFull: Twelve rulers walked the same ground and came back with the same facts; the difference was not information. Caleb stilled the people before Moses and urged them to go up at once and possess the land, because they were well able to overcome it (Numbers 13:30). The Most High had said that the land was His gift to the children of Israel (Numbers 13:2), so the stature of the men in it did not matter. Caleb was not playing any games and was not shook; he was about that business, ready to go and take the land, because he understood the land had already been promised. When the whole congregation wept and spoke of a captain to take them back to Egypt, Joshua and Caleb rent their clothes and spoke to all the company: the land they had passed through was an exceedingly good land; if the Lord delighted in them He would bring them into it; they were only not to rebel against the Lord or fear the people of the land, who were bread for them, because their defence had departed from them and the Lord was with Israel (Numbers 14:6-9). All the congregation called for them to be stoned, and the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle (Numbers 14:10).

That is what the obedience cost: public contradiction of a settled majority, faith and courage while the leaders around them were shook with doubt and fear. There has to be something different about a man in the matter of faith, because a faithless spirit does not profit the nation at all, and a man cannot keep company with men who will not go up. The Lord’s own words fix the standard: His servant Caleb had another spirit with him and had followed Him fully (Numbers 14:24).
judgmentFull: None of that generation would come into the land except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun (Numbers 14:30). Every other man numbered from twenty years old and upward died in the wilderness at a year for a day, and their children went in (Numbers 14:29-33). Out of all the people who came out of Egypt, only these two saw the land. Caleb at eighty-five asked for the mountain with the giants on it: he was as strong that day as on the day Moses sent him, as his strength was then so was it for war, and he asked for the mountain the Lord had spoken of that day, where Joshua had heard the Anakims were and the cities great and fenced; if the Lord was with him he would drive them out. Hebron became Caleb’s inheritance because he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel (Joshua 14:10-14).

The record praises the source of that strength rather than the man: the Lord gave strength also to Caleb, and it remained with him to his old age, so that he entered upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for a heritage, so that all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord (Ecclesiasticus 46:9-10). Everybody does not get that, and strength is shown when a man is going through something, not when everything is good. Joshua succeeded Moses, a man in whom the spirit was, was set before Eleazar the priest and all the congregation and given some of the honour of Moses in their sight, and he divided the land he had been the first to say could be taken (Numbers 27:18; Joshua 14:6). Mattathias recalled both of them at the end of his life: Caleb received the heritage of the land for bearing witness before the congregation, and Joshua was made a judge in Israel for fulfilling the word (1 Maccabees 2:55-56).

text.text: And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.
Send thou men, that they may search the land of Canaan, which I give unto the children of Israel: of every tribe of their fathers shall ye send a man, every one a ruler among them.
And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes:
And they spake unto all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land.
If the Lord delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which floweth with milk and honey.
Only rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the Lord is with us: fear them not.
But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel.
But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went; and his seed shall possess it.
Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me,
Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.
But as for you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness.
And your children shall wander in the wilderness forty years, and bear your whoredoms, until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness.

And now, behold, the Lord hath kept me alive, as he said, these forty and five years, even since the Lord spake this word unto Moses, while the children of Israel wandered in the wilderness: and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old.
As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in.

Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the Lord said.
And Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance.
Hebron therefore became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite unto this day, because that he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel.
The Lord gave strength also unto Caleb, which remained with him unto his old age: so that he entered upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage:
That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.
And the Lord said unto Moses, Take thee Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the spirit, and lay thine hand upon him;

Then the children of Judah came unto Joshua in Gilgal: and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite said unto him, Thou knowest the thing that the Lord said unto Moses the man of God concerning me and thee in Kadesh–barnea.
Jesus for fulfilling the word was made a judge in Israel.
Caleb for bearing witness before the congregation received the heritage of the land.
